input: Write a due diligence memo on Rippling

red_flags.claim: Competitive-conduct litigation remains material: the reviewed federal order allowed some Deel false-advertising counterclaims to proceed while staying or dismissing others. This was not a finding of liability.
Founder-governance diligence: the SEC imposed sanctions on Parker Conrad for conduct at his former company, Zenefits. This historical action was not against Rippling.
Employee-review warning: recent displayed Glassdoor reviews describe burnout and overwork. These are self-selected employee reports, not proof of company-wide conditions or a worsening trend.

Financing-verification gap: the reported $250 million Series H is supported by an aggregator entry rather than an issuer filing or company announcement in the reviewed evidence; do not underwrite it as confirmed capital.

traction.claim: Company claim reported by Reuters: Rippling served more than 20,000 customers as of May 9, 2025. A newer verified customer count was not established.

Company claim, website reviewed as of November 9, 2026: named customer references include Blank Street Coffee, Chess.com, Barry’s and Y Combinator. These references do not establish contract size or current revenue contribution.

missing_fields: financial_signals: Audited financial statements, recognized annual revenue, current profitability, cash balance, burn rate and runway were not verified.
financial_signals: A current independently verified headcount, comparable headcount growth series, and recent layoff totals were not established.
team: Notable executive departures during November 9, 2024–November 9, 2026 were not verified; this does not mean none occurred.
funding: Primary confirmation, closing documentation and valuation for the aggregator-reported August 2026 Series H were not verified.
legal_and_regulatory: Complete current procedural status and final outcomes of the Deel and Runlayer disputes were not established beyond the specific documents described.
legal_and_regulatory: Rippling-specific regulatory enforcement and sanctions/OFAC exposure were not verified; no clean screening result is implied.
reputation: A longitudinal employee-review rating trend was not established from the reviewed snapshots.
traction: A current customer count, quantified customer-count growth and material partnership agreements were not verified.

legal_and_regulatory.claim: In People Center v. Deel, No. 25-cv-02576-CRB, Rippling alleged corporate espionage and Deel asserted counterclaims. The September 25 order compelled arbitration of certain counterclaims, stayed computer-access and RICO counterclaims, and partly granted dismissal while allowing some false-advertising claims to proceed. Allegations remain distinct from findings.

In Deel’s separate Delaware action against People Center d/b/a Rippling, the court denied Deel’s motion to disqualify Rippling’s counsel. That procedural ruling did not resolve the underlying competitive-conduct allegations.

Anysource d/b/a Runlayer sued People Center d/b/a Rippling, alleging trade-secret misappropriation, unfair competition and breach of contract, and seeking injunctive relief and damages. These are complaint allegations, not adjudicated misconduct.

A Montana regulator-hosted notice from customer LumenAd/Pathlabs reported unauthorized logins to a recipient’s Rippling account and possible personal-information exposure. It does not establish a platform-wide Rippling compromise or a regulatory enforcement action.

Historical founder matter, not Rippling enforcement: the SEC found that Zenefits and its former CEO Parker Conrad violated Securities Act Section 17(a)(2). Conrad was ordered to pay a $160,000 civil penalty and $350,000 disgorgement, plus interest.

reputation.claim: Glassdoor snapshot reviewed as of November 9, 2026: 3.6/5 across 1,310 employee reviews, with 66% recommending the company and a 3.0 work-life-balance rating. Displayed November reviews praise challenging work and growth but also describe burnout and overwork; no historical ratings trend was established.

G2 snapshot reviewed as of November 9, 2026: 4.7/5 across 15,108 customer reviews. Positive themes include usability and consolidated HR workflows; recurring complaints include navigation, learning curve, setup and support accessibility, with individual complaints about accumulating module costs. Some displayed reviews are explicitly incentivized.

Critical press: Reuters reported Runlayer’s allegation that Rippling misused licensed software information to build a competing product. Rippling rejected the claims as fabricated; the report did not establish liability.

output.verdict: Rippling has a broad integrated product platform, recognizable customer references and substantial primary-confirmed financing; Sacra’s revenue estimates suggest meaningful scale but are not audited financial results. Before investing, prioritize financial quality and cash burn, confirmation of the aggregator-only 2026 financing, and the Deel/Runlayer disputes, alongside targeted checks on the founder’s historical regulatory record and employee-reported burnout.

financial_signals.claim: Sacra estimate: Rippling reached $1 billion in annualized revenue in March 2026, versus $850 million at year-end 2025, growing 78% year over year. These are third-party annualized estimates, not audited recognized annual revenue.

Reuters reported Rippling was not profitable as of May 9, 2025. Conrad said the company would need to be profitable before going public; this does not establish its profitability or IPO plans as of November 2026.

Aggregator snapshot: Tracxn listed 7,700 employees in the record verified November 8, 2026. The underlying measurement date was not supplied, so this should not be treated as a verified payroll count or comparable growth series.
Company claim: the Series G announcement stated Rippling was hiring across all roles as of May 9, 2025. This is a dated hiring signal, not confirmation of current hiring levels.

team.claim: Forbes identifies Parker Conrad and Prasanna Sankar as Rippling’s cofounders in 2016. Sankar served as CTO until 2020 before leaving to found 0xPPL; that departure falls outside the requested two-year window.
The company leadership page reviewed as of November 9, 2026 lists Parker Conrad as cofounder/CEO, Matt MacInnis as president/CPO, Albert Strasheim as CTO and Adam Swiecicki as CFO.

Company announcement: Adrian Ludwig joined as chief security officer. His prior roles included director of Android security at Google, CISO/chief trust officer at Atlassian, and chief architect/CISO at Tools for Humanity.

business.claim: Company description as of review: Rippling sells employers a unified workforce-management platform spanning HR, payroll, IT and finance, including tools to onboard, pay and manage employees and contractors globally.
Sacra describes a B2B SaaS model with per-employee, per-month subscription charges varying by selected module; customers commonly start with HR/payroll and add IT or finance products.
Company claim as of review: Rippling has an international office footprint spanning four continents, with San Francisco among its listed offices.

funding.claim: Reuters reported a $200 million financing led by Coatue at a $13.5 billion valuation, announced April 22, 2024.

Company-confirmed Series G: $450 million at a $16.8 billion valuation, with agreements to repurchase up to $200 million of employee/former-employee equity. Named investors included Elad Gil, Sands Capital, GIC, Goldman Sachs Alternatives, Baillie Gifford and Y Combinator. This is the latest primary-confirmed valuation established in the review.

Aggregator-only report: Captables, citing FundBat, lists a $250 million Series H dated August 6, 2026, led by Coatue Management. Captables explicitly describes database-listed evidence rather than an issuer filing; primary confirmation and a round-specific valuation were not established.
